problem.statement: Reviews with release r1 got 13 of 40 development reviews wrong: type_changed×3, field_removed×4, field_renamed×3, required_added×2, enum_value_removed×1.

hypothesis: If the change-review skill also runs interface_compat (a recursive structural diff of contract_before vs contract_after that blocks removed/renamed fields, type changes, unit/format/constraint changes, enum value removals, and requiredness changes while treating annotation-only changes and new optional fields as safe), then breaking interface changes (type_changed, field_removed, field_renamed, required_added, enum_value_removed and similar unseen kinds such as unit or nested-field changes) will be sent back with the correct dot-path field, raising accuracy above the current ~0.675 without increasing blocked safe changes; this is falsified if held-out accuracy does not rise, any breaking change is approved, or safe changes are blocked beyond the margin.
expected_benefit: Fewer approved breaking changes, with safe changes still approved.
possible_regressions: Each review runs one more step
The development cases only contain top-level field changes; nested-path handling (e.g. tolerance.lower) is untested against labels
Held-out change kinds (unit changes, nullability, bound changes, enum additions, format changes) have unknown labels; severity choices for them are judgment calls
The list of meaning-bearing x- extensions is a heuristic; unrecognised extensions that change meaning would only be advisory

change.summary: Added candidate/validators/interface_compat.mjs (id 'interface_compat'). It walks both schemas recursively through properties and items, building dot paths from the contract root. Blocking: field removed (reported as field_renamed if an added field has an identical schema), type set changed (including nullable), enum value removed / enum added / enum dropped, const changed, field became required or new required field, field became optional, and changes to non-annotation keywords such as x-unit, format, minimum/maximum, length, pattern, additionalProperties, plus x- extensions whose names suggest meaning (unit, scale, precision, timezone, currency, etc.). Advisory only: optional field added, enum value added, default changed, other x- extensions. Ignored: description, title, examples, deprecated and similar annotations. Development check: accuracy 1.0 (60/60), 0 of 38 breaking approved, 0 of 22 safe blocked, no errors.
